# Native receipt contract review data

These are hand-authored synthetic lifecycle/model traces for [N0-02's authoritative receipt contract](../../../docs/engine/native-contract.md#receipt-admission-retention-and-reconciliation), drafted on 2026-10-16 for [issue 8](https://github.com/whoodes/namtab/issues/8). They are review data: no engine, executable test harness, adopted public schema or successful NG0/model-test result is supplied. The contract owns rules; this directory owns local example provenance and integrity only.

- `valid-lifecycle.json` follows a managed launch through a lost admission ACK, identity-only reconciliation, duplicate lookup, changed-body refusal, full OS creation and independent exit/drain/acceptance facts. It also consumes a rejected next sequence without dispatch.
- `valid-retention.json` contains independent branches for volatile binding loss, restart and surviving-runner reconciliation, exact expiry, receipt compaction, retired namespaces, lost cursors and refusal when receipt storage is full.
- `valid-cancellation.json` contains independent queued, partial-takeover and in-flight unknown traces. Cancellation has its own admitted identity; its ACK does not imply target rollback or process death.
- `invalid-cases.json` describes forbidden claims or transitions against named valid branches. These JSON values are adversarial proposals, not executable patches or a second error vocabulary.

All IDs, bodies, arguments, clock ticks, control events and facts are invented, including any apparent ACK/prompt text. No process is executed. There are no user recordings, secrets, environment values, personal paths, upstream code or copied conformance data. Bodies/encoded bytes appear only as explicit **synthetic volatile** review inputs; they do not authorize durable input capture. Exact delivery extents assume authorization to disclose these synthetic extents. The local SHA-256 manifest hashes complete public fixture files for integrity, never actual request bodies or low-entropy user input. No dependency or project license is adopted.

The traces use the finite `n0-receipt-model/0` profile defined in the contract, canonical decimal strings for counters/ticks, and an injected trusted clock. Each independent branch starts from its own stated initial state; clocks and quotas are not shared across files/branches. `dispatch_start_count` counts logical external dispatch attempts for the named original operation; successful OS creation/write counts are separate. `expected` values are hand-authored proposed oracles. Facts not mentioned remain unchanged; a query or refused repeat never adds a dispatch. `operation` IDs and recorded principal bindings come from the service; none is a caller's grant. Omitted production wire fields are not wildcard authority: each branch explicitly assumes exact authorized subject/context/profile preconditions unless it challenges one.

The future V01–V03 model must independently encode transitions, enumerate clock/crash/scheduling cuts and challenge RC01–RC10 before treating these oracles as executable assertions. In particular, move a crash across the admission/dispatch-intent/OS-effect/result-record boundaries, delay an old controller frame, lose a volatile binding and remove old receipts. Correct an erroneous oracle through review of the authoritative contract and explain the reason before updating integrity hashes; do not regenerate expectations from an implementation merely to make it pass.

[manifest.json](manifest.json) records provenance, requirements/assertion mappings and SHA-256 hashes for the JSON data. Existing identity examples, the shared fixture manifest, historical source pins and original X4/EA1 FAIL evidence remain untouched. JSON parsing, integrity checks and strict documentation checks establish only static consistency.
